_Do you want to join a global leader in renewable energy infrastructure investment? Do you thrive with investment analysis, structured problem-solving, and translating complex analyses into strategic decisions? Then Copenhagen Infrastructure Partners (CIP) is the perfect place for you. We are currently looking for a Senior Associate to join our Group Investments and Financing team.

_**The team

**The Group Investments and Financing team is responsible for CIP Holding's balance sheet investment activities and capital allocation priorities, providing decision support to the CFO, CIP management, and CIP's owners. We work as a closely integrated team, delivering high-quality investment analyses and recommendations in collaboration with the responsible Partner and CFO as well as stakeholders across CIP. Our work supports major investment decisions and plays an important role in shaping CIP's long-term growth and strategic direction.

**The role

**As our new Senior Associate, you will help support CIP Holding's investment activities from analysis through to execution. This is an investment-focused role that combines well-developed analytical and strategic capabilities with practical project management and stakeholder engagement. You will work closely with the responsible Partner, the CFO, and colleagues across CIP, with direct exposure to senior stakeholders and strategic investment decisions.

You will join a highly motivated environment of talented colleagues with backgrounds from investment banking, private equity, and strategy consulting. The role offers significant responsibility early on and great opportunities for professional development.

You will thrive in a busy environment, balancing multiple priorities while consistently delivering high-quality work.

**Responsibilities will consist of, but are not limited to:

**

• Support CIP Holding's investments and strategic projects across CIP-managed funds, affiliated GPs, and new CIP companies

• Contribute to the development and refinement of the CIP Holding investment strategy, including capital allocation frameworks and long-term balance sheet planning

• Support the evaluation and execution of tactical allocation decisions, including analysis of investment and divestment opportunities

• Conduct investment analysis, valuation modelling, market assessments, and due diligence on new opportunities

• Support the negotiation of commercial and legal terms with funds, counterparties, and co-investors, alongside the responsible Partner and legal teams

• Manage project timelines, workstreams, and stakeholders across multiple parallel initiatives, ensuring clear ownership and follow-through

• Prepare investment recommendations, decision materials, and presentations for senior stakeholders and the Board

• Structure complex problems and perform thorough analysis to support strategic decision-making

• Collaborate across finance, legal, business development, and investor relations to support transaction execution and strategic initiatives

• Support ad hoc analyses, board materials, and special projects for the Partners and senior team members

**You

**We are looking for a motivated and collaborative professional with a Master's degree in Finance, Economics, Business, or a related discipline, combined with approximately 2-4 years of relevant experience from investment banking, private equity, management consulting, corporate finance, or a similar analytical environment.

CIP offers an international, intellectually stimulating, and high-performance environment. We are looking for a motivated, detail-oriented, and analytical professional who is focused on developing themselves within strategic investments and capital allocation.

**Key qualifications include:

**

• Strong financial and strategic acumen, with solid valuation, investment analysis, and financial modelling skills

• Experience supporting transaction processes, due diligence, and investment-related analyses

• Ability to structure complex problems and evaluate opportunities and risks across a range of scenarios, with solid numerical skills and attention to detail

• Skilled in project management, with experience overseeing processes, bringing stakeholders together, and tracking multiple workstreams

• Experience with, or interest in, negotiating commercial and legal terms

• Advanced Excel and PowerPoint proficiency, with the ability to produce high-quality decision materials

• Interest in fund structures, GP/LP dynamics, and infrastructure or renewable energy investments is an advantage

• A proactive and structured approach, with ownership of deliverables and the motivation to move projects forward

• Skilled at building productive relationships and collaborating across teams and functions

• Excellent written and verbal English skills

**The process

**Please apply online as soon as possible as applications will be processed on an ongoing basis. For questions related to the role, please reach out to our Talent Acquisition team at recruitment@cipfs.com. We do not include CV's and Cover Letters sent by email.

As we continue to improve our candidate experience, diversity and avoid unconscious bias, please avoid having a photo in your CV. We commit to an inclusive recruitment process and equality for all applicants.

Please be aware that we will not accept speculative CV submissions for any of our roles from recruitment agencies, and any unsolicited candidate submissions will be exempt from any payment expectations and ownership.

**Building value that matters

**Founded in 2012, Copenhagen Infrastructure Partners P/S (CIP) today is the world’s largest dedicated fund manager within greenfield renewable energy investments and a global leader in offshore wind. To date, CIP has developed and constructed more than +50 greenfield renewable projects around the world. CIP is developing a greenfield project portfolio of ~160GW total, and ~16 GW is in operation or under construction. CIP manages 13 funds and has to date raised approximately EUR ~35 billion for investments in energy and associated infrastructure from more than ~200 international institutional investors.

CIP has a multinational team of ~500 full-time employees with extensive experience and knowledge within the fields of renewable energy project development and regulated infrastructure. In addition, CIP has a broad range of competencies within corporate finance, mergers & acquisitions, engineering, construction, project development, and project management.

CIP has built a prominent investment team capable of originating proprietary investment opportunities and executing projects and investments based on the team’s industrial background, large industrial network, and extensive experience in structuring, executing, and managing investments within energy infrastructure. Headquartered in Copenhagen, CIP also operates from key locations across the globe, including offices in Hamburg, Munich, London, Utrecht, New York, Tokyo, Melbourne, Luxembourg, Kuala Lumpur, Seoul and Singapore. In addition, CIP has 17 local project offices globally.

For more information, visit www.cip.com.

Your closest partners will be development project teams and headquarters-based study groups. You will also work with affiliates, external partners across the value chain, key opinion leaders and Health Authorities – bringing perspectives together so decisions are clear and projects keep their momentum.

You will join dedicated and highly engaged colleagues in a flexible, collaborative and cross-functional setting. Your expertise will be trusted, and your voice will count in shaping the clinical pharmacology strategy of the projects you lead.

Additionally, you will help others grow, sharing your knowledge and mentoring colleagues to build Clinical Pharmacology capabilities. In return, you will broaden your own perspective through close work across the development value chain and with global stakeholders.

The Aarhus Laboratory Astrochemistry Group is seeking applications for a postdoctoral position in laboratory astrochemistry under supervision of Prof. Liv Hornekær at the Department of Physics and Astronomy at Aarhus University.

Job description
The successful applicants will participate in the experimental research activities under ERC Synergy Grant IRAstro and DNRF Center of Excellence for Interstellar Catalysis – InterCat. This combined project aims at elucidating how molecules on interstellar dust grain analogue surfaces organize, react and dissipate energy under low temperature and low pressure conditions mimicking dense interstellar dust and molecular clouds. The applicant will use low temperature scanning tunneling microscopy (STM), temperature programmed desorption, and (single molecule) IR spectroscopy to follow in situ reactions leading to complex molecule formation on realistic dust grain analogue surfaces. Close collaboration with theoreticians, observers and the experimental astrochemistry groups at Aarhus University and at the nodes of collaborative partners is expected.

The job includes:

• Mapping of catalytic pathways and reaction rates on interstellar dust grain analogue surfaces using STM, TPD, and RAIRS. 
• development, maintenance and troubleshooting on various experimental UHV setups
• participating in maintenance of the group laboratories.
• data analysis and writing scientific publications.
• supervision of PhD, Master and bachelor students.
• project administration, such as writing reports etc.
 
Qualifications
Candidates should have a PhD degree in physics or similar field, with strong experience in experimental surface science, UHV techniques, catalysis/reactions on surfaces and atomic scale characterization. A background in laboratory astrochemistry is preferred.

The ideal candidate has good collaboration skills and is also able to work independently.

About IRAstro - Molecular Quantum Dynamics in Low-Temperature Astrochemistry 
The ERC Synergy project IRAstro brings together leading researchers in physics, chemistry, and astrochemistry to uncover how molecules behave and react under the extreme conditions of interstellar space.

Recent observations from the James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) reveal the complexity of low temperature molecular ices frozen out on interstellar dust grains in regions where new stars and planetary systems are formed. Interpreting these observations requires a deeper understanding of the fundamental physical and chemical processes that govern molecular behaviour at temperatures close to absolute zero.

IRAstro addresses this challenge by combining cutting-edge laboratory experiments, advanced instrumentation, and first-principles theory. The project focuses on the quantum dynamics of molecules in low-temperature condensed phases - a frontier area essential for understanding how chemical complexity arises in space.

https://phys.au.dk/irastro

About InterCat – Center for Interstellar Catalysis 
InterCat is a center of excellence supported by the Danish National Research Foundation. The center is situated at the Department of Physics and Astronomy and at the Interdisciplinary Nanoscience Center at Aarhus University in Denmark, at Leiden Observatory at Leiden University in the Netherlands and Niels Bohr Institute at University of Copenhagen in Denmark. See https://phys.au.dk/intercat/ for further details.

The scientific aim of the Center for Interstellar Catalysis is to determine whether the production of the molecular building blocks of life, e.g., sugars, amino acids, fats and DNA bases, predates the formation of stars and planets, and occurs at the extremely low temperatures and pressures found in interstellar space. InterCat thus aims to determine the molecular starting conditions for the origin of life across the universe.

InterCat brings together research teams within surface science, nanoscience, heterogeneous catalysis and experimental and observational astrochemistry.

jobs.occupation: Sequencing Platform and Service Manager at Section of Microbiology
jobs.description:
Department of Biology at Faculty of Science, University of Copenhagen is looking for a Sequencing platform and service manager with effect from 1 December 2026.

  About us
 At the Section of Microbiology, we are working to understand and exploit the immense functional diversity and adaptive potential of natural microbial communities using cutting-edge molecular techniques including high throughput DNA sequencing, cell-sorting, single-cell detection, and real time biofilm formation at the Bioflux centre.

  Tasks
 The position is for coordinating sequencing operations and laboratory workflows into a broader role combining service management, method development, data management, customer coordination, technical advisory functions, and platform administration.

  Your tasks will include

   	
• Managing sequencing service contracts, including coordination with internal and external stakeholders and follow-up on service delivery. 	
• Acting as the main contact person for sequencing platform providers and coordinating technical and operational matters related to the platforms. 	
• Developing and implementing new analytical protocols, including workflows for 16S sequencing and analysis using PacBio. 	
• Taking responsibility for sequencing data storage, organization, management, and accessibility. 	
• Performing and overseeing data cleaning and preparation as part of the sequencing and analysis workflow. 	
• Serving as the direct contact for external customers and collaborators, including coordination of sequencing requests, requirements, timelines, and technical questions. 	
• Developing, updating, and providing guidance on laboratory and sequencing protocols to ensure consistent procedures and quality. 	
• Providing technical advice to service users and colleagues on DNA-related techniques, sample preparation, sequencing requirements, and troubleshooting.   We expect

   	
• A relevant Master's degree or equivalent academic qualification within, for example, microbiology, molecular biology, biotechnology, biochemistry, bioinformatics, or a related field. 	
• Practical experience with molecular biology and DNA-based laboratory methods, including DNA extraction, sample preparation, PCR, and sequencing workflows. 	
• Experience with next-generation sequencing technologies and preferably both short- and long-read sequencing approaches. 	
• Experience with or knowledge of amplicon sequencing, particularly 16S rRNA gene sequencing. Experience with PacBio sequencing is an advantage. 	
• Experience with sequencing data handling, quality control, organization, and management. 	
• Experience coordinating technical services, laboratory workflows, research infrastructure, platforms, or projects. 	
• The ability to advise researchers and service users on technical questions and translate scientific requirements into practical workflows. 	
• Good IT and data-management skills. Experience with bioinformatic workflows or sequencing-data analysis is an advantage. 	
• Good written and verbal communication skills in English.   We offer
 We offer an independent and varied position in an internationally oriented research environment where you will have the opportunity to contribute directly to the development and operation of sequencing services and research infrastructure.
 You will work closely with researchers, technical staff, students, external collaborators, service users, and technology providers and will have opportunities to develop your expertise within sequencing technologies, laboratory and analytical workflows, data management, and research infrastructure management.

  The Section of Microbiology provides a collaborative working environment with access to advanced technologies and research activities spanning microbial ecology, microbiomics, microbial interactions, environmental microbiology, and related areas.

  Place of employment
 The place of employment is at Section of Microbiology, Department of Biology, University of Copenhagen. We offer creative and stimulating working conditions in dynamic and international research environment.

  Terms of salary and employment
 The position is full-time with an average working time of 37 hours per week. The position is a fixed-term position limited to a period of 1 year. The starting date is 1 December 2026 or by agreement.

  Employment will be as Special Consultant under The Circular on the Collective Agreement concerning Academics in the state sector concluded between the Danish Ministry of Finance and Akademikerne (the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations). There will be an opportunity to negotiate supplements based on qualifications. You can read more about salary levels in the state sector www.loenoverblik.dk (in Danish). 

  Your application
 If you are interested in the position, please submit your electronic application, including attachments, via the UCPH Job Portal (click the “APPLY NOW” link at the bottom of the job posting). 
 Your application should include:

   	
• Letter of application addressing the requirements (max. one page). 	
• Curriculum Vitae 	
• A certified/signed copy of certificate(s) of education   Application deadline is 22 October 2026.

  Interviews will take place week 43-44.

  The University of Copenhagen seeks to reflect society and encourages applications irrespective of personal background.

  Further questions

  Any questions about the position may be directed to Professor. Søren Johannes Sørensen, sjs@bio.ku.dk.   

  The University of Copenhagen has established a new shared administrative structure, which is still being implemented. This entails ongoing changes and development of, among other things, work processes and areas of collaboration.
